Project Description:
Grasim Industries Limited (GIL), Ganjam is one of the leading chlor-alkali producers in India. In order to meet the increasing water demand, GIL has planned to set up a 5 MLD SWRO desalination plant. It also helps as an alternative sustainable solution to prevent excessive withdrawal of groundwater. 

The activities of the proposed desalination plant involve development of facilities like: (i) Desalination process plant, (ii) Intake channel from Rushikulya River mouth, (iii) Collection sump and (iv) Discharge of brine reject through outfall diffuser in the Bay of Bengal.

Seawater intake of about 12.5 MLD will be withdrawn through intake channel. Brine reject of 7.5 MLD will be discharged back through an outfall pipeline. Another 0.5 MLD of other saline water generated from existing RO plant will be mixed with brine reject and discharged together in sea.
Description: CRZ clearance form
Project Name: Setting Up 5 MLD Desalination Plant for Grasim Industries Limited at Ganjam in Odisha State
Alternative Site Examined: NO
Alternative Site Description: The intake and outfall locations are fixed considering Rushikulya River, Olive Ridley Turtle nesting, Potagada fort and Bay of Bengal. Justification of no other alternatives are as follows,  •	Upstream of the Rushikulya River contains freshwater and it's utilized by villagers. •	Northern coast of the Rushikulya River mouth consists nesting ground for turtles. •	South of the plant location includes sand dunes with vegetation. •	East of the Rushikulya River mouth doesn't have any ESA.

Project Description:
Koraput - Rayagda (Singapur Road) (164 Kms.) line popularly known as K- R line of East Coast Railway is a single line section, which connects to the Raipur/ Sambalpur-Vizianagaram line at Singapur Road stations and Kottavalasa- Kirandul line at Koraput Station, it is an important Rail Link to Bailadilla Mines. The line traverses through scenic hills of Eastern Ghats from a height of 934m above MSL to 245 m above MSL through hinterland of Orissa State. The construction of K-R Line was started in 1982-83, and the line was opened to Goods traffic in 1996-97 and finally for passenger traffic in Dec.1998. Electrification of Koraput-Damanjodi section was commissioned consequent on setting of the Aluminium Plant at Damanjodi by M/s NALCO Ltd.

Project Description:
The manufacturing process of the Ferro chrome comprises following major steps of operations, namely:
i)Briquetting of chrome ore fines by setting up dryer, mixer and briquetting machine.
ii)Setting up SAF for production of HC Fe-Cr alloy with slag through Electro- Carbothermic reduction of chromite charge. 
iii) Casting of alloy & slag in bed under shed. Chipping, sizing and packing of finished product over concrete floor and under shed. Slag to be ground and jigged using water to separate alloy metal & stored in slag yard and to be used in construction work after TCLP test.
iv) Furnace off-gas will be cleaned in jet venturi scrubber & to be burnt in combustion chamber to produce heat which will be utilized to produce steam to generate power for the process.
v) When needed furnace off-gas will be flared.
vi) Scrubber sludge will be utilized in making briquette.
vii) Production of 96,000 TPA high Carbon Ferrochrome & 10 MW Power generation from furnace off gas on 50.29 ha of land.

Project Description: NALCO, as part of the company future expansion program is proposing for Brownfield expansion of aluminium smelter capacity from 4.6 LTPA to 9.57 LTPA by addition of 5th Pot Line of approx.0.5 MTPA capacity. Mining Life of Mine Other Info:
The present mining plan has been prepared for working upto 220 mtr depth with mine life of 23 
 years including 2 years of construction period. As per approved Mine Plan, mine opening has been considered  from 2025 and mine shall be closure shall be done by 2053. After commencement of mine operation scientific study will be carried out for mining of balance resource. ML will be valid for 30 years i.e upto 2055.
Mining Type of Mining Other Info: OB excavation by shovel and dumper combination and blasting shall be done in OB to loose the material for handling. In coal, surface miner will be deployed for extraction of coal, so no blasting will required.
Mining External Dumping Remarks: No external dump has been proposed in the approved Mining Plan. Only temporary dump has been proposed., where OB will be kept and shall be used for back-filing the void created due to mining.
Mining Internal Dumping Remarks: No internal dump has been proposed in the approved Mining Plan. Only temporary dump has been proposed., where OB will be kept and shall be used for back-filing the void created due to mining.
Mining Topsoil Dumping Remarks: Temporary Top soil dump has been proposed in the approved Mining Plan. Top soil shall be spread over the Backfilled area of the excavation pit, for plantation.
Mining Quarry Other Info: A final void of 17 mtr depth of 25 mtr of water body will be left for recharge of water and to promote aquatic life in the area. Other excavated areas will be filled up with OB.
Mining Transportation Mode From Pithead: Railway siding has been proposed within the mining lease area. Coal from the mine pit shall be transported through HEMM/ dumpers to the pit head CHP . The crushed coal shall be transported to RCC Silo through belt conveyor system (CHP). Railway wagons shall be loaded through rapid loading Silo.
Mining Transportation Mode From Loading: Coal is proposed to be transported through rail mode only to Vedanta plants. Any surplus coal if available, it will be sold in the market from pit head stock.  Initial for about two years of mine operation, coal shall be transported by road to Vedanta plant located at 25 km from mine. Later coal shall be transported via Rail mode after commissioning of the Railway siding. Although the company is targeting to start the railway siding at the earliest.

Iron Ore is a mineral substance mined / extracted from Earth’s Crust; it is used as raw material for Iron / Steel production. Iron Ore Beneficiation is the process of improving the quality of low grade iron ore by removing impurities like alumina & silica and increasing its iron content.  This process improves the chemical, physical and metallurgical characteristics of the ore to make it a more desirable feed for iron making furnaces. There are several techniques used in iron ore beneficial process, depending on the nature of the ore and its impurities.

Project Description: The outcrop detailed map of Notara-Tangipatana-Sankhei area shows significant potentiality for REE mineralization, not only in terms of bedrocks, but also soil samples. Accordingly, based on the mineral prospectivity of the area w.r.t. REE and RM, a G3 block in Notara-Tangipatana-Ikiri block has been proposed for FS: 2025-2026. The proposed work components will involve 2.4 sq. km. topographic survey and detailed mapping on 1:2000 scale, pitting/trenching and systematic regolith and bed rock sampling. Bedrock sampling will be carried out from hard rocks exposed in the area whereas, in the soil covered area, regolith samples will be collected at tentative 50 m x 50 m grid interval through pitting or from the exposed regolith profile. Due to high REE values of soil samples, the target for regolith samples has been kept as 100, which will be preferentially collection through systematic pitting/trenching.

Project Description: Kesharpur South copper prospect is located approximately 25 km NNW of Baripada ( Gap area between Kesharpur and  Madansahi blocks) in the southern margin of the Singhbhum Copper belt, falling in SOI  T.S No. 73 J/12. The rock types of the area are quartz-biotite-chlorite- schist, hornblende-biotite-schist and quartzite of the Singhbhum Group constituting the main country rocks. They are later intruded by granite, vein quartz and dolerite dykes. The Romapahari granite/ Mayurbhanj granite in the area is represented by leucocratic granite, hornblende biotite granite gneiss and augen gneiss. All the rocks are again intruded by Newer Dolerites. The megascopic structural features marked in the area are foliations, joints and lineations. The general strike of the gneisses on the western side varies from N20°W - S20°E to N30°W -S30°E, dipping 40° to 70° towards NE.

Project Description:
The proposed construction of the 3rd and 4th railway lines between Sason and Sarla Stations Is a critical infrastructure project under the Sambalpur Division of East Coast Railway. The existing Sambalpur-Jharsuguda double line section has already reached more than 150% of its designed line capacity, resulting in congestion, delays, and inefficiencies in the movement of both freight and passenger trains. This stretch is particularly important as it serves as a junction for goods trains operating between the Sarla-Jharsuguda/IB line and the Talcher-Sambalpur section.

The project will directly benefit major industries such as Vedanta Alumina Ltd., Jindal Steel & Power Ltd., Bhushan Power & Steel, and Shyam Metaliks, which rely heavily on rail transport for both raw material inflow and finished product dispatch. Strengthening this corridor through additional lines will reduce bottlenecks, enhance freight movement, and support regional economic growth.

Project Description: Dudhiasol West Copper Prospect is located approximately 30 km NNW of Baripada (1 km North west of Kesarpur Cu deposit) in the southern margin of the Singhbhum Copper belt, falling in SOI T S No 73J/12. The proposed Dudhiasol west block is located west of the Dudhiasol east  block, FS 2019-20 and North west of Nimaidihi block FS 2024-25. The rock types of the area are quartz-biotite-chlorite- schist, hornblende-biotite-schist and quartzites which constitute the main country rocks. They are later intruded by granite, vein quartz and dolerite dykes. The Romapahari granite/ Mayurbhanj granite in the area is represented by leucocratic granite, hornblende biotite granite gneiss and augen gneiss. The eastern part of the area is mostly covered by laterites. The western part is dominated by hornblende-granite-gneiss and massive leucocratic granite which form low and irregular mounds in the otherwise flat and soil covered tract.

Project Description: The entire iron ore mineral deposit of ML-227 (3.34 ha) is falls inside the forest land. Considering the demand of the Iron Ore by the SAIL’s Steel Plants for captive use, the exploitation & Mining of iron ore from 3.34 ha is very much essential to cater iron ore demand of SAIL’s steel plant. Since the occurrence of the above mineral is site specific, which happens to fall in forest land, the area is required for diversion to win these minerals.
Description: Forest clearance form
Project Name: Proposal for diversion of entire 3.34 ha of forest land (including 0.68 ha earmarked for safety zone) within ML-227 Mining Lease under Section 2 (1) (ii) of Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980 for Iron Ore Mining and ancillary activities in favour of M/s Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL)- Kalta Iron Mines in Toda RF, Koira Tahsil, Sundargarh District of Odisha
Alternative Site Examined: Not applicable as the project or activity is site specific
Mining Life of Mine Other Info: Life of Mine will vary after detailed exploration to be done after Stage-II FC.
Mining Type of Mining Other Info: Iron ore extracted through mechanised means. Iron ore, mineral reject and waste in mining benches will be loosen through drilling using 100 mm diameter drills and blasting using low density (LD) cartridge explosives and excavation of blasted material by Excavator, dumper- truck combination. Rock breaker will be utilized for size reduction of large boulder to less than 300mm and finally manually sized and sorted for size reduction and classification for lump (+10 mm - 40 mm) and fines (-10 mm), hence there will be no mining loss envisaged. Considering the available sub-surface data UPL has been designed for economically and feasibly extraction of iron ore.
Mining Blasting Other Info:
No mining activities have been commenced till date in the lease area and in forth coming
proposal period open cast mechanised mining method will be adopted 100 mm dia holes will be
drilled with the help of wagon drills for blasting The working benches will be of 6 m height and 6
m wide Combination of shovel and tippers will be utilized for winning or ore and handling of
waste
Mining Transportation Mode From Loading: by road through 10/25 tonne dump truck
Mining Transportation Mode Other Info: Roxy Railway Siding  of SAIL will use for loading of material

The project aims to ensure long-term water security, improved public health, and socio-economic development of the rural population by providing drinking water conforming to IS:10500 standards. Project Description:
The project involves the installation of solar panels with bore well arrangements in five villages—Malipasi and Saramundi villages under K. Balipal Gram Panchayat, and Dalki, Ratanmara, and Pitanau villages under Hadagarh Gram Panchayat in Keonjhar District. This initiative is part of the RWSS Mega Piped Water Supply (PWS) scheme designed to provide safe and reliable drinking water to 200 villages under Hatadihi Block.
Under this project, solar-powered pumping systems will be installed along with bore wells to ensure a sustainable and uninterrupted water supply.
The bore wells will extract groundwater, which will then be pumped using the solar-powered system and supplied to the villages through the Mega PWS infrastructure. The project aims to improve access to safe and potable drinking water, enhance public health and sanitation, and reduce the burden on villagers—particularly women and children—who often travel long distances to collect water.
